title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from lunar navigation ambitions to the latest in satellite cancellations. Meanwhile, the budget is looking a bit more generous for space resilience, and the competition is heating up as various players vie for dominance in the sector.

themes.title: Lunar Navigation Takes Shape
themes.body: Northrop Grumman is setting its sights on the lunar navigation market with a new guidance system derived from the Webb telescope. This could signal a shift in how we approach lunar missions, blending terrestrial tech with celestial navigation.

themes.title: Satellite Cancellations Raise Eyebrows
themes.body: SES and Eutelsat's decision to cancel GEO expansion satellites highlights the shifting dynamics in satellite deployment strategies. As LEO services gain traction, the GEO market might need to rethink its value proposition.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition of the need for robust capabilities. This funding could pave the way for advancements that enhance national security in orbit.

themes.title: Competition in the Launch Arena
themes.body: With SpaceX setting a date for its first Starship version 3 launch, the competition among launch providers is intensifying. The stakes are high as other rocketeers scramble to capture market attention and secure contracts.
